messages:
maria: heads up — canary deployment of text-gen v2.3.4 is throwing crashloops and we're seeing a spike in 500s from customers, started ~2m ago. rolling back? :frowning:
ops-bot: incident created INC-20260315-37, paging oncall ashley-oncall and sre-lead. escalation policy: prod-pager.
ashley-oncall: on it — paging me as oncall. which cluster/namespace?
maria: prod cluster, namespace=prod, deployment=text-gen. I tried `kubectl get pods -n prod | grep text-gen` — paste below:
```
text-gen-canary-1   0/1 CrashLoopBackOff  12   3m
text-gen-canary-2   0/1 CrashLoopBackOff  9    3m
text-gen-frontend-5 1/1 Running           0    1h
```
```
kubectl get hpa -n prod | grep text-gen
text-gen        50/10   300%   1%   50      20       300s
```
ryan: whoa hpa target looks totally wrong (1%). looks like a bad manifest or helm values pushed a wrong HPA target. that explains the huge scale and node pressure. canary pods also show `exec format error` in logs?
maria: logs from one crashloop pod:
```
2026-03-15T14:02:11Z ERROR runtime: exec format error: failed to start container process
stack: fork/exec /app/bin/text-gen: exec format error
```
```
ashley-oncall: ok two issues: 1) canary image appears incompatible (wrong architecture or bad build) causing CrashLoopBackOff; 2) HPA target misconfigured so it scaled up way beyond max expected. first priority: stop traffic to canary to stop customer impact. next: rollback canary and patch HPA.
ryan: agree — flip feature flag to stop routing to canary. Maria can you flip LD flag `enable-new-tokenizer` to false?
maria: doing flag flip now via LaunchDarkly UI (shared session). will post confirmation.
maria: flag `enable-new-tokenizer` -> false. traffic to canary should drop within ~20s.
ops-bot: LD flag change detected for key enable-new-tokenizer by maria.
ashley-oncall: checking frontend routing metrics... 45s later — 5xx rate dropping but still above baseline. proceeding with rollback for deployment.
ashley-oncall: running: `kubectl -n prod rollout undo deployment/text-gen --to-revision=3`
deploy-bot: started rollout undo for deployment-text-gen in prod by ashley-oncall (rollout id: r-2026-03-15-37).
maria: HPA patch attempt to restore sane values: `kubectl -n prod patch hpa text-gen --type=merge -p '{"spec":{"targetCPUUtilizationPercentage":65,"minReplicas":2,"maxReplicas":10}}'`
ryan: good — also check minReplicas wasn't set to 0. if min=0 during rolling update it can race to zero.
maria: minReplicas was 0 — patched to 2. desired replicas decreasing now.
ashley-oncall: nodes showing pressure on node-abc: memory 98%, pod evictions happening. I want to cordon+drain one saturated node after we reduce replicas further. draining now will risk short-lived 503s but should free resources. anyone object?
sre-lead: go ahead, coordinate with deployment stickiness. ensure we don't drain multiple nodes at once.
ashley-oncall: `kubectl cordon node-abc && kubectl drain node-abc --ignore-daemonsets --delete-local-data --force`
```
node/node-abc cordoned
evicting pod text-gen-canary-2
evicting pod text-gen-canary-1
```

maria: rollback rollout undo completed, new pods coming up from v2.3.3. `kubectl get pods -n prod | grep text-gen` ->
```
text-gen-5   1/1 Running  0  20s
text-gen-6   1/1 Running  0  18s
```

ashley-oncall: HPA now: `text-gen  3/3  65%  65%  3  3  30s` — desired replicas down to 3. customer 5xxs trending back to baseline.
ryan: what's root cause? looks like two separate mistakes in same deploy: bad image + accidental hap values in helm values. we should add a deploy guard to validate HPA sensible ranges and image sanity.
maria: confirmed `exec format error` traced to build pipeline producing amd64 artifact but tag was used for arm64 infra in this region — build matrix bug.
sre-lead: mitigation summary: 1) flipped LD flag to stop traffic to canary, 2) rollout undo to v2.3.3, 3) patched HPA to reasonable values and minReplicas=2, 4) cordoned/drained saturated node to relieve pressure. customer impact: elevated 5xx for ~8 minutes, targeted subsets only (api/generate), no data loss.
ops-bot: incident INC-20260315-37 status -> RESOLVED by ashley-oncall. duration 00:12:32.
ashley-oncall: handing off to postmortem owner @sre-lead for follow-up. please capture action items.
sre-lead: action items: [1] Add CI check that HPA targetCPU within sane bounds (>=20% <=80%) for any helm values pushed to prod. [2] Build pipeline: enforce multi-arch image tags and validate image entrypoint runs in each target arch. [3] Add deploy-time canary kill-switch that automatically routes traffic away if >5% 5xx in first 3 min. [4] Run chaos/drain playbook to ensure safe node draining during incidents. assign owners and due dates.
maria: will open PRs for (1) and (2) and link to incident.
ryan: thanks team — nice quick coordination. posting final metrics: 5xx spike peaked at +420% above baseline, returned to baseline after rollback/patching.
ashley-oncall: closing thread. please add any additional notes to INC-20260315-37 ticket.
sre-lead: noted, will write up full postmortem and include timelines, commands used, and follow-ups.
